'''2000 Decipher World Championship''' was the fifth Star Wars CCG World Championship, played 5–7 October 2000 at [[DecipherCon 2000]] in the Doubletree Resort and Conference Center, Kissimmee, Florida. [[Matt Sokol]] (United States) defeated [[Yannick Lapointe]] (Canada) in the Final Confrontation.<ref name="wp">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game Star Wars Customizable Card Game], Wikipedia</ref><ref name="sokol">[https://web.archive.org/web/20041026224145/http://www.trandosite.mcmail.com/iv16.htm Matt Sokol interview], [[Trandosite]] (25 October 2000)</ref><ref name="sched">[https://web.archive.org/web/20061009205800/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/schedule/ DecipherCon 2000 schedule], Decipher (Wayback 9 October 2006)</ref>

[[File:DecipherCon 2000 SWCCG champion plaque.jpg|thumb|right|280px|2000 World Champion plaque]]
[[File:DecipherCon 2000 tournament hall.jpg|thumb|right|280px|Main hall, 6 October 2000]]

[[Trandosite]] called the weekend the largest World Championship field to that date.<ref name="trando-wf">[https://web.archive.org/web/20050517110350/http://trandosite.mcmail.com/wf00p2.htm History of the World Finals], [[Trandosite]]</ref> The constructed pool was [[Premiere - Death Star II]]. [[Death Star II (expansion)|Death Star II]] had been published on 19 July 2000. It covers the Battle of Endor and the second Death Star.<ref name="ds2">[[Death Star II (expansion)]]</ref> Wikipedia and ''Star Wars Insider'' 52 list 72 Day 1 players.<ref name="wp" /><ref name="insider">''Star Wars Insider'' 52 (2000)</ref> Francis K. Lalumiere, writing from the floor on 5 October, put 170 competitors in the main hall for Day 1.<ref name="fkl2">[https://web.archive.org/web/20010107221700/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/reports/fkl2.html Mighty Jabba Sails Across the Atlantic], Francis K. Lalumiere, Decipher (Wayback 7 January 2001)</ref> [[Tim Guzman]] wrote that Day 1 started with 170 and that the top 38 advanced.<ref name="guzman-d1">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-10-info-brokers-dcon-day-one-reportd1317/ info-brokers-dcon-day-one-report], Tim Guzman, Decktech (10 October 2000)</ref> Sokol was player 36 on Day 1. He lost the first final game and won the second. Combined score 2 (+5) to 2 (−5).<ref name="sokol" /><ref name="jls3">[https://web.archive.org/web/20001117011300/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/reports/jls3.html Matt Sokol, 2000 Star Wars CCG World Champion!], Jean-Luc Simard, Decipher (Wayback 17 November 2000)</ref>

This was the last Star Wars Worlds Decipher ran at a company convention. On 3 October 2001 [[Warren Holland]] cancelled [[DecipherCon 2001]].<ref name="holland">[https://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/Special_message_from_Decipher_CEO_Warren_Holland_70685.asp Special message from Decipher CEO Warren Holland], TheForce.Net (3 October 2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261010073714/https://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/Special_message_from_Decipher_CEO_Warren_Holland_70685.asp Internet Archive]</ref>

== Format ==

* '''Environment:''' [[Premiere - Death Star II]]
* '''Site:''' [[DecipherCon 2000]], Doubletree Resort and Conference Center, Kissimmee, Florida
* '''Dates:''' 5–7 October 2000 (Thursday–Saturday); the convention continued through 8 October
* '''Field:''' 72 Day 1 (Wikipedia / ''Insider'' 52); 57 Day 2 with posted Final Totals (Decipher results page)<ref name="wp" /><ref name="d2">[https://web.archive.org/web/20001026043505/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/events/results/starwars.html DecipherCon 2000 Day 2]</ref><ref name="insider" />

[[Justin Pakes]] directed the Star Wars rooms.<ref name="tennet">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-13-deciphercon-2000-juz-beer-and-cardsd1338/ deciphercon-2000-juz-beer-and-cards], Alex "Greedo" Tennet, Decktech (13 October 2000)</ref> Day 1 was eight games. The top 38 joined pre-qualified champions on Day 2.<ref name="dc00fin">[http://decipher.com/tournaments/deciphercon2000/swfinalists.html DecipherCon 2000: Star Wars CCG Qualifiers], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010308110320/http://decipher.com/tournaments/deciphercon2000/swfinalists.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="guzman-d1" /> Day 2 was eight games (4 Light / 4 Dark). Twelve advanced to Day 3. Day 3 reset those twelve for four games (2 Light / 2 Dark). The top two played the Final Confrontation.<ref name="d3">[https://web.archive.org/web/20010303120030/http://decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/events/results/starwars3.html DecipherCon 2000 Day 3]</ref>

The last Day 2 slot was [[Dominic Gaudreault]] 10 (+70). [[Martin Akesson]] 10 (+69) missed by one differential.<ref name="d2" /> On Day 3, [[Kevin Shannon]]'s Game 2 Dark vs [[Steve Brentson]] was a '''Modified Win by 14''' (+1 victory point). A full win there would have moved Shannon past Sokol on the cut math. That example is on [[Tournaments#2000 World Championship — Sokol, Shannon, and a modified win]].<ref name="d3" />

== Qualifiers ==

Seventy players reached the World Championship: the 1999 champion [[Gary Carman]], 4 Open champions, 3 Continental champions, 24 Regional champions and 38 wildcards from Day One. The Coruscant regional had co-champions, and the European Championship winner was [[Martin Akesson]] ([[2000 European Championship]]).<ref name="dc00fin" />

== Day 1 ==

Day 1 was the open wildcard. Unqualified players played eight games for 38 seats on Day 2.<ref name="dc00fin" /><ref name="guzman-d1" /> Play started hours late. Sokol wrote that the open began about 1 p.m., three hours after the posted time.<ref name="sokol-dt">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-11-sokols-dcon-2000-reportd1327/ sokols-dcon-2000-report], Matt Sokol, Decktech (11 October 2000)</ref> [[John Arendt]] waited three hours past the published start.<ref name="arendt">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-09-deciphercon-beedos-report-day-1-2d1314/ deciphercon-beedos-report-day-1-2], John Arendt, Decktech (9 October 2000)</ref> [[Hayes Hunter]] later said first pairings went up at 1 p.m. and the day ran until 2 a.m.<ref name="hayes-pds2-ops">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qJuistFFk9M&t=2794s SWCCG PDS2: Hayes Hunter Worlds 2023 Champion Interview], BillBisco2 (10 May 2025), 46:34–46:54. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-qJuistFFk9M Internet Archive]; [https://web.archive.org/web/20261016010406/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qJuistFFk9M watch-page snapshot] (Wayback 16 October 2026).</ref> [[Charlie Herren]] called Day 1 the most poorly run tournament he had seen.<ref name="herren" /> [[Paul Todd Feldman]] said the tournament software was not working properly and that pairings took a long time.<ref name="feldman-pds2-ops">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b9f9tNBiU2I&t=2428s SWCCG PDS2: Paul Todd Feldman Interview], BillBisco2 (29 May 2025), 40:28–40:37. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-b9f9tNBiU2I Internet Archive].</ref>

[[Peter Di Biasio]] went undefeated and won the Day 1 Swiss.<ref name="tennet" /><ref name="muller">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-11-10-05-00d1323/ 10-05-00], Brian Muller, Decktech (11 October 2000)</ref> [[Bastian Winkelhaus]] finished second at 7–1.<ref name="winkelhaus-tr">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-14-deciphercon-by-bastian-winkelhausd1340/ deciphercon-by-bastian-winkelhaus], Bastian Winkelhaus, Decktech (14 October 2000)</ref> [[Hayes Hunter]] finished third on Day 1.<ref name="hayes-tr">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-14-hayess-dcon-game-reportd1341/ hayess-dcon-game-report], Hayes Hunter, Decktech (14 October 2000)</ref> [[Dominic Gaudreault]] finished fourth.<ref name="dom">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-12-dom-goes-to-floridad1333/ dom-goes-to-florida], Dominic Gaudreault, Decktech (12 October 2000)</ref> [[Geoff Snider]] finished 12th and made the cut.<ref name="snider">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-08-deciphercon-2000d1309/ deciphercon-2000], Geoff Snider, Decktech (8 October 2000)</ref> Sokol finished 36th (Dark 4–0, Light 1–3).<ref name="sokol-dt" /> [[Tim Guzman]] finished 34th of the field he counted as 170.<ref name="guzman-d1" />

Sokol wrote: "Day 1 was the hardest tourney I have ever played in. It turns out that all the good players from around the world wanted to show up for this event."<ref name="sokol-dt" /> Arendt wrote that Day 1 competition was fierce because so many seats were open. He named the German crew, the Quebecers, and the Albany crew as the hard pockets.<ref name="arendt" /> [[Mike Fitzgerald]] called it "the biggest tournament of the year."<ref name="fitz">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-09-icemans-dcon-2000-reportd1310/ icemans-dcon-2000-report], Mike Fitzgerald, Decktech (9 October 2000)</ref>

=== Disqualifications ===

Decipher deck-checked lists during the open. A list that did not match the 60-card deck ended the player's Worlds run.<ref name="tennet" /><ref name="sokol-dt" />

[[Jonny Chu]] was 5–2 going into game 8 when a check removed him. Sokol and [[Brian Terwilliger]] were at the table when the call came.<ref name="sokol-dt" /><ref name="tennet" /> Chu later said he a 59-card list.<ref name="chu-pds2">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JLkMOP3rLQ8&t=1341s SWCCG PDS2: Jonny Chu Interview], BillBisco2 (28 April 2025), 22:21–22:49</ref> [[Steven Lewis]] was 3–0 after game 3 when a check removed him.<ref name="lewis">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-15-how-to-get-disqualified-at-worldsd1349/ how-to-get-disqualified-at-worlds], Steven Lewis, Decktech (15 October 2000)</ref> Tennet also named [[Michael Girard]] and [[Kim Caton]] among the Day 1 disqualifications.<ref name="tennet" /> [[Michael Raveling]] was removed after game 5 for a 61-card list (Grey Squadron 1 written as Gold Squadron 1).<ref name="raveling">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-10-orlando-florida-2000d1318/ orlando-florida-2000], Michael Raveling, Decktech (10 October 2000)</ref>

=== Cut and seating ===

[[Michael Riboulet]], the Naboo Regional winner, missed his flight. Decipher seated [[Mike Kessling]], the Naboo runner-up, in that Day 2 chair. [[Gabriel Alonso]], 39th on Day 1, took the remaining alternate seat.<ref name="tennet" />

Players who missed the 38 included [[Alex Tennet]] (5–3), [[Justin Desai]] (5–3, about 41st), [[Charles Hickey]] (about 10th with +20, short of the cut), [[Jeff Anderson]] (86th on differential), [[Joe Olson]], [[Joe Horbey]], [[Brian Terwilliger]], and [[Chris Jank]] (4–4).<ref name="tennet" /><ref name="desai">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-15-15-drunk-men-at-dennys-worldsd1346/ 15-drunk-men-at-dennys-worlds], Justin Desai, Decktech (15 October 2000)</ref><ref name="hickey">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-14-mr-hickey-goes-to-floridad1343/ mr-hickey-goes-to-florida], Charles Hickey, Decktech (14 October 2000)</ref><ref name="anderson-pds2">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qErV_KgLAgA&t=1337s SWCCG PDS2: Jeff Anderson Interview], BillBisco2 (9 August 2025), 22:17–25:28</ref><ref name="snider" /><ref name="twigg">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-12-twigg-at-d-con-2kd1331/ twigg-at-d-con-2k], Brian Terwilliger, Decktech (12 October 2000)</ref><ref name="jank">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-13-coruscant-operative-reportingd1337/ coruscant-operative-reporting], Chris Jank, Decktech (13 October 2000)</ref>

Horbey played Tennet in game 6 with an Akesson-style [[You Can Either Profit By This / He Must Pay|Profit]] list. Tennet won by about 20.<ref name="tennet" /> Olson played Snider in game 1 (Hidden Base / Tatooine Celebrating).<ref name="snider" /> Anderson drove overnight from Alabama, started late with the registration line, and stayed to watch the Final Confrontation on the big screen.<ref name="anderson-pds2" />

== Day 2 ==

Day 2 opened near on time, about an hour late by Winkelhaus's clock.<ref name="winkelhaus-tr" /> Eight games, four per side. Twelve advanced.

[[Clint Hays]] led the table 14 (+85). [[Kyle Craft]] was second 14 (+65). [[Martin Falke]] was third 13 (+54). Sokol finished eighth 12 (+6) on [[Jonny Chu]]'s Hidden Base X-wing Light and his own Bring Him Before Me Dark ("the beast").<ref name="d2" /><ref name="sokol-dt" /> Winkelhaus started 5–0, then lost his last three to Akesson, Craft, and Carman, and finished 22nd 9 (+42).<ref name="winkelhaus-tr" /><ref name="d2" /> Hunter finished 15th 10 (+54) after a modified loss to [[Paul Todd Feldman]] in game 8.<ref name="d2" /><ref name="hayes-tr" />

[[Team Albany]] built Sokol's Day 3 [[ISB Operations / Empire's Sinister Agents|ISB Operations]] list overnight after Day 2. [[Brian Terwilliger]], [[Chris Terwilliger]], [[Jonny Chu]], [[Art Wright]], and [[Aaron Kingery]] sat with him on that build.<ref name="sokol-dt" /><ref name="sokol" /> Sokol's Light for Days 2–3 was Chu's Hidden Base X-wing swarm. Sokol later cut Luke and added inserts for the Final Confrontation.<ref name="sokol-dt" /><ref name="chu-pds2" />

== Final Confrontation ==

The match was played in a closed room. The audience watched on a large screen next door, with commentary by [[Joe Alread]], [[Kyle Heuer]], and [[Kendrick Summers]]. Jean-Luc Simard's Decipher report and Sokol's Decktech report are the play-by-play sources.<ref name="jls3" /><ref name="sokol-dt" /> [[Justin Pakes]] and [[Joe Helfrich]] judged.<ref name="dcon-fc-jdg">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q0sFxQ2i3Hk&t=832s DecipherCon 2000 SWCCG World Championship Final Confrontation], Player's Council (20 February 2022), 13:52–14:35. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-Q0sFxQ2i3Hk Internet Archive]; [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008004102/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q0sFxQ2i3Hk watch-page snapshot] (Wayback 8 October 2026).</ref> [[Mark Tuttle]] called play-by-play, with color commentary by Alread.<ref name="dcon-fc-comm">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q0sFxQ2i3Hk&t=82s DecipherCon 2000 SWCCG World Championship Final Confrontation], Player's Council (20 February 2022), 1:22–1:32. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-Q0sFxQ2i3Hk Internet Archive]; [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008004102/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q0sFxQ2i3Hk watch-page snapshot] (Wayback 8 October 2026).</ref> [[Chris Craig]] did rulings throughout the tournament.<ref name="dcon-fc-jdg" />

Game 1: Sokol [[Hidden Base / Systems Will Slip Through Your Fingers|Hidden Base]] (X-wings / Numbers) against Lapointe [[Bring Him Before Me / Take Your Father's Place|Bring Him Before Me]]. Sokol's Light list went in at 59 cards; he added [[Civil Disorder]] at registration and the deck had no Luke. Lapointe won by 20.<ref name="jls3" /><ref name="sokol-dt" />

Game 2: Sokol [[ISB Operations / Empire's Sinister Agents|ISB Operations]] (walkers / Sandwhirl) against Lapointe's Super Falcon list. Sokol needed at least 21 Force of differential. An [[Abyssin Ornament]] left him on 25 Life Force; Lapointe drew his last card. Combined: Sokol 2 (+5), Lapointe 2 (−5).<ref name="jls3" />

Sokol later won the Sunday team constructed event with Chu and both Terwilligers.<ref name="sokol-dt" /><ref name="sokol" />

The Player's Council posted the original Decipher streaming video of both games.<ref name="dcon-fc">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q0sFxQ2i3Hk DecipherCon 2000 SWCCG World Championship Final Confrontation], Player's Council (20 February 2022). Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-Q0sFxQ2i3Hk Internet Archive]; [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008004102/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q0sFxQ2i3Hk watch-page snapshot] (Wayback 8 October 2026).</ref>

[[File:DecipherCon 2000 Worlds Final still.jpg|640px|link=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q0sFxQ2i3Hk]]

[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q0sFxQ2i3Hk Watch the Final Confrontation] (1 hour 21 minutes). Convention, guests, side events, and the surviving official photographs are on [[DecipherCon 2000]].

After the match, Decipher recorded a post-match interview with Sokol and Lapointe. Derek Brooks provided the footage; brandon baity (NanashiStudios) posted it on 21 August 2018.<ref name="dcon-iv">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ECUW3AIAH3A DecipherCon 2000 Championship Match Interview], brandon baity (NanashiStudios) (21 August 2018). Footage by Derek Brooks. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ECUW3AIAH3A Internet Archive].</ref>

== Recollections ==

Players writing in October 2000 and speaking in later interviews treated the weekend as the Death Star II constructed peak. The expansion had been out for three months. Honor of the Jedi had already punished Hunt Down. No Escape from Enhanced Jabba's Palace was on sale at the convention and was not legal for Worlds.<ref name="ds2" /><ref name="sokol" /><ref name="hayes-pds2">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qJuistFFk9M&t=2200s SWCCG PDS2: Hayes Hunter Worlds 2023 Champion Interview], BillBisco2 (10 May 2025), 36:40–38:50. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-qJuistFFk9M Internet Archive]; [https://web.archive.org/web/20261016010406/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qJuistFFk9M watch-page snapshot] (Wayback 16 October 2026).</ref><ref name="olson-pds2">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A-yqKSMt6gE&t=2223s SWCCG PDS2: Joe Olson Interview], BillBisco2 (12 May 2025), 37:03–39:25</ref>

[[Hayes Hunter]] called the event "sort of a pinnacle I think of the game." Death Star II had come out in the summer. Worlds was in October. "A three-month window… but everybody remembers that time period."<ref name="hayes-pds2" /> Two weeks after the final, Sokol told Trandosite: "Death Star 2 changed the game so much. You can get so much force fast now… it is insane."<ref name="sokol" /> [[Jonny Chu]] said Hidden Base X-wings work because of Death Star II: without [[Honor Of The Jedi]], Hunt Down is hard.<ref name="chu-pds2" /> [[Joe Olson]], then 15, flew in off a Portland Grand Slam win, played last-minute Hunt Down, and "just got crushed." He said Honor of the Jedi "just like crushes Hunt Down."<ref name="olson-pds2" />

Winkelhaus told Trandosite in May 2000 that Worlds are "the biggest and best tournament every year."<ref name="trando-iv3">[https://web.archive.org/web/20041026204829/http://www.trandosite.mcmail.com/iv3.htm Bastian Winkelhaus interview], [[Trandosite]] (26 May 2000)</ref> After Day 2 in Kissimmee he wrote that it was a great experience.<ref name="winkelhaus-tr" /> Fitzgerald called it the biggest tournament of the year.<ref name="fitz" /> Arendt wrote that Day 1 was fierce because so many seats were open.<ref name="arendt" />

Sokol went in expecting Day 2, maybe Day 3, not a title. "What kept me going was all my friends on Team Albany."<ref name="sokol" /> Friday night Chu handed him Hidden Base X-wings. Sokol's own Light had gone 1–3 on Day 1.<ref name="sokol-pds2">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jFXqTc1jkNc&t=2707s SWCCG PDS2: Matt Sokol, Worlds 2000 Champion Interview], BillBisco2 (6 May 2025), 45:07–48:21. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-jFXqTc1jkNc Internet Archive]; [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008224620/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jFXqTc1jkNc watch-page snapshot] (Wayback 8 October 2026).</ref> After the Final Confrontation he heard friends screaming in the next room: "it was the greatest feeling in the world."<ref name="sokol" /> He later said Chu and Brian Terwilliger were the reasons he won.<ref name="sokol-pds2" /> The next day Team Albany won the team event. Sokol called it "the best weekend ever."<ref name="sokol-pds2" />

Hunter said Day 3 was a poor, anticlimactic miniature Swiss and that Sokol "totally deserved it."<ref name="hayes-pds2" /> He later said Day 1 was poorly run: first pairings went up at 1 p.m., and play ran until 2 a.m.<ref name="hayes-pds2-ops" /> [[Paul Todd Feldman]] said the tournament software was not working properly and that pairings took a long time.<ref name="feldman-pds2-ops" /> Feldman called the weekend "a cluster" and said 2000 "looked like a company that wanted to go bankrupt."<ref name="feldman-pds2">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b9f9tNBiU2I&t=5014s SWCCG PDS2: Paul Todd Feldman Interview], BillBisco2 (29 May 2025), 1:23:34–1:27:26</ref> He finished 11th on Day 3 and then stopped playing.<ref name="feldman-pds2" /> Hunter said players walked behind tables and shared what opponents played.<ref name="hayes-pds2-scout">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qJuistFFk9M&t=3043s SWCCG PDS2: Hayes Hunter Worlds 2023 Champion Interview], BillBisco2 (10 May 2025), 50:43–51:12. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-qJuistFFk9M Internet Archive]; [https://web.archive.org/web/20261016010406/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qJuistFFk9M watch-page snapshot] (Wayback 16 October 2026).</ref> Olson said players with teams had a huge advantage, and that Sokol won because Team Albany worked together.<ref name="olson-pds2" />

[[Jeff Anderson]] played his only Decipher Worlds that weekend. He finished 86th on Day 1, missed the cut on differential, and watched Sokol versus Lapointe on the big screen with 25–30 people.<ref name="anderson-pds2" /> [[Steven Lewis]], after the Day 1 disqualification, wrote that he played so he could meet people from around the world. "Did I do that at Worlds? ABSOLUTELY!"<ref name="lewis" />
